I get it. Sometimes you just want to munch on something. No worries. Some of my favourites to recommend are:

  • Homemade popped corn. Great snack since it has that crunch and plus it's a whole grain. You also don't need to add any extra fat: just pop it in a brown paper bag in the microwave. No oil needed! Sprinkle some of your favourite seasonings and you're good to go!

  • Gim. It's roasted seaweed. The store-bought brands are a bit higher in sodium but it can be made easily at home also. It definitely has that savoury flavour you're after.

  • Bell Peppers. A little bit sweet with lots of crunch.

Happy snacking!
ELI5: Why does stretching feel so good?

When we sleep our heart rate slows down. Blood does not flow freely to the muscles, which in turn leaves them oxygen deprived and with waste to be disposed of. Our muscles and joints might also be stiff from lack of activity.

Stretching - * elongating and contracting muscles all around your body* - makes the stiffness go away, the blood will flow quicker again, blood pressure to rise, which results in more fresh oxygenated to the brain. Sure feels good :)

Carl Linnaeus structured a system by which he hoped to classify all the flora and fauna of the world. In furtherance of this goal, he arranged for his graduate students to travel the world, observing and collection specimens. These students, known as the "Apostles of Linnaeus" did much of the world's pioneering work in naturalism/biology. The project got off to a rocky start, though.

Linnaeus' first student, Christopher Tärnström applied - with the recommendation of Linnaeus - for employment as ship’s priest on one of the Swedish East India Company ships in 1744. The application was not successful. Tärnström won employment the following year, on 16 October 1745 and departed on the ship Calmar early in 1746. His travel was financed by his position as a ship’s priest but his research was to be funded by a scholarship. This scholarship was secured by Linnaeus and The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, and was supposed to be paid on arrival at Canton, China. This condition never came to pass for Tärnström.

Tärnström died on the island of Pulo-Condore, off the coast Vietnam, where he had worked for just two months. He never sent back a single specimen. Tärnström’s first wife had given him a child before her death in 1741. His second wife bore him two children, one in his absence. After Tärnström’s death, his widow found herself in financial difficulties and Linnaeus felt some obligation towards the family’s plight. Because of this difficulty, Linnaeus only selected young unmarried men for the long scientific voyages.

Sources? Well, if you can't trust The IK Foundation, who can you trust? They'll even sell you an edition of Tärnström’s journal. The story has made it into a secondary source, Linnaeus: The Complete Naturalist, pg. 185-186, but this anecdote seems not to have entered English sources until recently!
